name: Vienna
distance_from_hq_phrase: Vienna is 10-15 minutes from our home base in Fairfax
geographic_anchor_paragraph: Vienna, VA sits at an interesting electrical crossroads. The town runs roughly between the Wolf Trap area to the west, the Tysons-edge to the east, Hunter Mill Road as its southern spine, and the Maple Avenue corridor at the center.
audience_descriptor: Residential homeowners in Vienna, VA and surrounding Northern Fairfax County neighborhoods including Vienna Woods, Hunter Mill, Tysons-edge, and Wolf Trap.

other_areas_paragraph: Outside Vienna, we serve Fairfax, McLean, Oakton, Tysons, Burke, Annandale, Falls Church, and the rest of Fairfax County. We also cover DC and Montgomery County, MD (Rockville, Bethesda, Chevy Chase, Potomac).

housing_patterns.title: 1950s-1970s split-levels & ranches
housing_patterns.neighborhood_examples: Vienna Woods, Country Club area, neighborhoods near Westwood
housing_patterns.context_paragraph: Built with 100-amp panels and circuits sized for the appliances of the era — toaster, fridge, color TV, a window unit if you were lucky. Fast-forward to 2026: induction range, central AC, two refrigerators, a tankless water heater, and an EV charger in the garage. Modern load patterns overwhelm circuits the original builder never planned for.
housing_patterns.symptoms: persistent breaker trips, warm outlets, dimming lights when large appliances start.

housing_patterns.title: 1970s-1990s colonials & traditionals
housing_patterns.neighborhood_examples: Hunter Mill District, Vienna proper, north of Maple Avenue
housing_patterns.context_paragraph: 200-amp service but wired with the now-deprecated aluminum branch wiring for a window in the mid-1970s, or with GFCI gaps in kitchens and bathrooms that predate the 1996 code requirement.
housing_patterns.symptoms: outlets that worked yesterday and don't today, intermittent power loss to one room, GFCIs that trip the moment a hairdryer plugs in.

housing_patterns.title: 2000s-2020s townhomes & newer detached
housing_patterns.neighborhood_examples: Tysons-edge, Wolf Trap area, newer subdivisions
housing_patterns.context_paragraph: Newer homes are not exempt. AFCI breakers (the arc-fault interrupters required by modern code) are sensitive by design and trip on any noisy load. Smart-home wiring done by the previous owner's "handy friend" can leave neutral wires bonded incorrectly.
housing_patterns.symptoms: failed dimmers, dead three-way switches, outlets that test fine but won't hold a plug.

troubleshooting.summary: Lights flicker when the AC or fridge kicks on
troubleshooting.body: Voltage drop. Often a loose neutral at the meter base or a damaged feeder. Common in older Vienna Woods and Country Club Hills homes built before 1980 — the service entrance is reaching the end of its life. Worth diagnosing soon: persistent voltage drops shorten the life of every motor in your house.

troubleshooting.summary: A breaker keeps tripping (more than once a week)
troubleshooting.body: The breaker is doing its job — something's wrong upstream. Usually an overloaded circuit (new microwave + toaster on the same line), a short in a wall outlet, or a failed breaker itself. We trace which of the three in 30-60 minutes.

troubleshooting.summary: An outlet or switch plate feels warm to the touch
troubleshooting.body: Stop using the circuit and call us today. Heat at a connection means resistance, and resistance behind drywall is how house fires start. Most common in 1970s-1990s Hunter Mill colonials with original wire-nut splices in junction boxes.

troubleshooting.summary: You smell burning plastic or "hot" electrical odor
troubleshooting.body: Treat this as urgent. Shut off the breaker for the affected area if you can identify it. We triage these calls to the earliest slot — typically same-day in Vienna. The cause is almost always overheated insulation at a loose connection.

troubleshooting.summary: Half your house has power, half doesn't
troubleshooting.body: An open neutral at the service entrance. Serious condition — it can fluctuate voltage between 50V and 200V and damage electronics. We test each leg of the panel and identify the failure point. Often a utility-side issue but we confirm before calling Dominion Energy.

troubleshooting.summary: Your EV charger throttles, trips, or warms the outlet
troubleshooting.body: EV charging puts continuous 30-50 amp draw on circuits that older Vienna homes weren't designed for. The cause is usually upstream of the charger — a feeder, a breaker, or a connection that can't sustain the load. Common in Wolf Trap and Tysons-edge homes where owners added a Level 2 charger to a pre-2010 panel.

most_common_problem_paragraph.troubleshooting: Two patterns dominate. In 1950s-1970s homes (Vienna Woods, Country Club Hills), the most common issue is circuit overload from modern appliances on original circuits. In 1970s-1990s homes (Hunter Mill, Vienna proper), the most common issue is intermittent power loss from aging connections in outlet boxes, panels, or junction boxes hidden in walls.

specific_problems_neighborhood_phrase.troubleshooting: Vienna has more EV drivers per square mile than most Fairfax County zip codes.
